items.informal_name: Taylor Algebra Homomorphism
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommSemiring R] → R → Polynomial R →ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a given element $ r $ in a commutative semiring $ R $, this is the $ R $-algebra homomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that sends each polynomial $ f $ to the composition $ f(X + r) $. It preserves addition, scalar multiplication, and multiplication of polynomials by substituting $ X + r $ into $ f $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Isomorphism for Polynomials over Commutative Rings
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommRing R] → R → Polynomial R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $, the Taylor isomorphism is an $ R $-algebra isomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that maps each polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $. This equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Isomorphism for Polynomials over Commutative Rings
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (r : R), ↑(Polynomial.taylorEquiv r) = Polynomial.taylorAlgHom r
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $, there exists an $ R $-algebra isomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that maps each polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $. This isomorphism preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $.

items.informal_name: The Taylor Shift Operator: Algebra Homomorphism vs. Linear Map
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (r : R) (a : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.taylorAlgHom r) a = (Polynomial.taylor r) a
items.informal_description:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $r \in R$, and $p$ a polynomial over $R$. Then
$$ (\text{Polynomial.taylorAlgHom } r)(p) = (\text{Polynomial.taylor } r)(p) $$
Here, `Polynomial.taylorAlgHom r` and `Polynomial.taylor r` are the Taylor shift operator $p(X) \mapsto p(X+r)$, viewed as an $R$-algebra homomorphism and an $R$-linear map, respectively.

items.informal_name: Renaming variables in multivariate polynomials
items.type:
{σ : Type u_1} →
  {τ : Type u_2} → {R : Type u_4} → [inst : CommSemiring R] → (σ → τ) → MvPolynomial σ R →ₐ[R] MvPolynomial τ R
items.informal_description: The $ R $-algebra homomorphism that renames variables in a multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ according to a function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, substituting each variable $ X_\sigma $ with $ X_{f(\sigma)} $ in the target ring $ R[\tau] $. This homomorphism preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $.

items.informal_name: Variable Substitution Homomorphism for Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
{σ : Type u_1} →
  {τ : Type u_2} →
    {R : Type u_3} → [inst : CommSemiring R] → (σ → MvPolynomial τ R) → MvPolynomial σ R →ₐ[R] MvPolynomial τ R
items.informal_description: The algebra homomorphism that substitutes each variable in $\sigma$ with a multivariate polynomial in $\tau$, defined by evaluating polynomials in $R[\sigma]$ using the given assignment $f : \sigma \to R[\tau]$ for variables. This operation preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by $R$, mapping a polynomial $P \in R[\sigma]$ to its evaluation with variables replaced by $f(\sigma)$. Equivalent to the evaluation homomorphism induced by the variable substitution $f$.

items.informal_name: Equality of Taylor Algebra Homomorphism and Taylor Series Expansion
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (r : R), ↑(Polynomial.taylorAlgHom r) = Polynomial.taylor r
items.informal_description: For a given element $ r $ in a commutative semiring $ R $, the Taylor algebra homomorphism $ \text{taylorAlgHom}_r: R[X] \to R[X] $ coincides with the Taylor series expansion linear map $ \text{taylor}_r: R[X] \to R[X] $, both of which send each polynomial $ f $ to the composition $ f(X + r) $. This equality asserts that substituting $ X + r $ into a polynomial preserves its algebraic structure as both an $ R $-linear map and an $ R $-algebra homomorphism.

items.informal_name: Taylor Expansion Formula for Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.taylor r) f = f.comp (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C r)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f $ in $ R[X] $ and any element $ r $ in the semiring $ R $, the Taylor expansion of $ f $ at $ r $ is equal to the composition of $ f $ with the polynomial $ X + r $, i.e., $ \text{Tay}_r(f) = f(X + r) $, where $ X $ denotes the indeterminate of the polynomial ring.

items.name: MvPolynomial.aeval_ite_mem_eq_self
items.type: {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] (q : MvPolynomial σ R) {s : Set σ} (hs : ↑q.vars ⊆ s) [(i : σ) → Decidable (i ∈ s)] : (MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => if i ∈ s then MvPolynomial.X i else 0) q = q

items.name: MvPolynomial.aeval_ite_mem_eq
items.type: {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] (q : MvPolynomial σ R) (s : Set σ) [DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ s] [DecidablePred fun x => ↑x.support ⊆ s] : (MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => if i ∈ s then MvPolynomial.X i else 0) q = ∑ x ∈ q.support, if ↑x.support ⊆ s then (MvPolynomial.monomial x) (q.coeff x) else 0

items.informal_name: Action of the Polynomial Shift Automorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] (t : R) (a : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.algEquivAevalXAddC t) a = (Polynomial.aeval (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C t)) a
items.informal_description: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $t \in R$. For any polynomial $p \in R[X]$, the action of the algebra automorphism `Polynomial.algEquivAevalXAddC t` on $p$ is given by the evaluation of $p$ at the polynomial $X+t$. This corresponds to substituting the variable $X$ with $X+t$ in the polynomial $p$.

items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence $ \text{algEquivCMulXAddC}_{a,b} $ corresponds to evaluating a polynomial at the linear expression $ aX + b $, where $ a $ and $ b $ are elements of a commutative ring $ R $. Specifically, for any polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, applying this equivalence yields the same result as substituting $ X $ with $ aX + b $ in $ f $ and evaluating via the canonical algebra homomorphism.

items.informal_name: Taylor Isomorphism for Polynomials over Commutative Rings
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommRing R] → R → Polynomial R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $, the Taylor isomorphism is an $ R $-algebra isomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that maps each polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $. This equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Isomorphism Induced by Linear Polynomial $aX + b$
items.type: {R : Type u_3} → [inst : CommRing R] → (a : R) → R → [Invertible a] → Polynomial R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $R$ and elements $a,b \in R$ with $a$ invertible, the linear polynomial $aX + b$ induces an $R$-algebra automorphism of $R[X]$. This isomorphism is given by composition with $aX + b$, with inverse given by composition with $\frac{1}{a}(X - b)$, since their composition yields the identity polynomial $X$.
